final_rationale: No genuinely new admissible evidence was added. The Actor mainly reframed the same record more narrowly and conceded the key weakness: the present file does not show that the disclosure issue for the named small-business onboarding segment was resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. That narrowing improves precision, but it does not cure the missing policy predicate. This is the distinction between caveated compliance and noncompliance here: caveated compliance would be plausible if the caveat were about follow-up monitoring or documentation after a satisfied launch predicate; it is not enough when the caveat is itself an unresolved pre-launch compliance condition. On the admissible record summarized here, the certification-as-compliant position is not supportable.
remaining_concerns: The affected small-business onboarding segment is named in two paid pilot commitments, which fits the policy's materiality trigger for a contractual customer segment or named launch use case.
The record still contains an open legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows a final disclosure determination or an approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering this limitation.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support overall readiness, but they do not satisfy the separate disclosure predicate for a potentially material segment weakness.
Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance support documentation and monitoring, but they do not substitute for compliance with the internal materiality/disclosure rule.
